answer: An agent economy resists sybils by binding each identity to one attestable secure element: a tamper-resistant chip holds manufacturer-signed key that cannot be exported, and ledger keeps an atlas of enrolled serial numbers, rejecting duplicates. The issuer enforces one signing secret per physical module, copying a key does not mint a new serial. A reef of clones must buy N chips, a linear cost; extra identities are unprofitable only while each epoch's reward is below the amortized per-chip rental plus enrollment fee. Stops cheap minting, not a wealthy buyer crossing that cost canyon.
